summary: Liang Cai is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology who studied under Daniel Boucher. In 2014, she held a junior scholar position at the University of Arkansas.

Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. In 2020, she was attested as a teacher of Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto.
Lili Zheng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, attested in 2011.

Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Lakshman Joo, held a post at the CNRS from circa 1948 to 1974, and taught André Padoux.

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós.

Limei Chi works in Buddhist studies and Sinology and studied under Jinhua Chen. As of 2026, she is attested as a faculty member at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Lin He (1902–1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from circa 1919 to 1926. He taught at National Tsing Hua University from circa 1931 to 1952 and instructed Jiyu Ren.
Lin Heng specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, attested in 2015.

Linda Hogan (born 1964) is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Trinity College Dublin in 1991. She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, where she served as Vice-Provost and Chief Academic Officer (2011–2016).
Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe, attested in 2001.
Linda Learman works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory, both attested in 2005.

Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993. She served as a research fellow at Taisho University, attested in 1983, and taught Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She completed an MA under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas and studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.

Lindy Li Mark (born 1932) is a scholar in Sinology and anthropology. She held positions as professor of anthropology at California State University, Hayward, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo, attested in 2014.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (circa 1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (circa 1966–1972), later holding a post at Tartu from circa 1969 to 2010.

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at Liverpool and Cambridge. He served at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), was Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and lectured at SOAS (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia (born 1971) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He held posts at INALCO, EPHE, KU Leuven, Lille 3, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Lisa Grumbach is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Stanford University, attested in 1996, and has served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and she studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.
